Abstract expression corresponding to Sanskrit kṣaṇika-phalatva: the fact or state of being an effect that is momentary. It pairs with skad cig ma'i rgyu yin pa (being a momentary cause) in discussions of instantaneous cause and effect.

Renders Sanskrit kṣaṇikaprayoga, a training or practical application characterized as momentary, i.e., accomplished in a single instant. It is naturally associated with the notion of complete enlightenment in one moment (skad cig gcig mngon rdzogs byang chub).

see_also: skad cig gcig mngon rdzogs byang chub
skad cig gcig gi rtogs pa

skad cig re re la.gloss: in each instant, at every moment

senses.gloss: in each instant, at every moment
senses.context: Adverbial phrase for Sanskrit pratikṣaṇam, marking something as occurring in every single instant, moment, or period. Equivalent in force to skad cig ma re re la.

skad cig re re la byung ba.gloss: arising in each moment, momentary arising

senses.gloss: arising in each moment, momentary arising
senses.context: Rendering Sanskrit pratikṣaṇotpāda, the term describes something that comes into being in every single instant, moment by moment. Used where production is said to occur in each successive period or instant rather than only once.

skad cig la 'jig pa'i don.gloss: the fact/meaning of disintegrating in a moment

senses.gloss: the fact/meaning of disintegrating in a moment
senses.context: Corresponds to Sanskrit kṣaṇa-bhaṅgārtha, the point or meaning that things break up (bhaṅga) within an instant (kṣaṇa). It names momentary disintegration as a topic or established meaning.
An enumeration of four principal languages, given as Sanskrit, Prakrit, Apabhraṃśa, and Pisachi. The phrase combines skad (language) with rigs (type, class) and chen po bzhi (the four great ones).

skad sor bzhag tu bzhag.gloss: the language was left as is

senses.gloss: the language was left as is
senses.context: Said of wording that is retained in its original form rather than altered or rendered anew, i.e., left just as it stood (sor bzhag). Here skad has the sense of language or wording.

skabs khyad par can yod pa'i bstan pa.gloss: teaching allowing occasion for something more special

senses.gloss: teaching allowing occasion for something more special
senses.context: A teaching with respect to which there remains an opening or occasion (skabs) for something more distinguished or special to be said. The phrase marks a doctrinal statement as not final in the sense that a further, more special point may still be introduced.

skabs dang po'i spyi don.gloss: general meaning of the first chapter

senses.gloss: general meaning of the first chapter
senses.context: A textual-commentarial rubric designating the overall or general presentation (spyi don) of the topics treated in the first chapter or section (skabs dang po) of a text. Used as a section title in expositions organized by chapter.

skabs 'dir dngos su bstan pa'i mtshan ny.gloss: meaning of the character-non-nature explicitly indicated on this occasion

senses.gloss: meaning of the character-non-nature explicitly indicated on this occasion
senses.context: A technical phrase identifying the sense of the 'non-nature of character' (mtshan nyid ngo bo nyid med pa) insofar as it is explicitly (dngos su) taught in the passage or context presently under discussion. The qualifier 'on this occasion' restricts the explanation to what the present passage directly sets forth, as distinct from what is indicated only implicitly or elsewhere.

skabs 'dir bstan.gloss: indicated on this occasion; indicated in this context

senses.gloss: indicated on this occasion; indicated in this context
senses.context: Said of what a text sets forth at the point currently under discussion, i.e., in the present passage or section (skabs). Frequently qualifies a term to distinguish the sense taught here from senses taught in other contexts.

see_also: skabs 'dir dngos su bstan pa'i mtshan nyid ngo bo nyid med pa'i don

skabs 'dir bstan gyi yid mngon.gloss: mental direct perception indicated on this occasion

senses.gloss: mental direct perception indicated on this occasion
senses.context: The particular kind of mental direct perception (yid kyi mngon sum) that is set forth in the passage presently under discussion, per Hopkins with reference to Dharmakīrti's Commentary on (Dignāga's) Compilation of Prime Cognition (tshad ma rnam 'grel, Pramāṇavārttika). The qualifier 'indicated on this occasion' delimits which mental direct perception is at issue in that context.
Used of something suited or proportionate to its occasion or place (skabs).
Rendering Sanskrit mṛṣṭa in the corpus marked {C} by Lokesh Chandra and Hopkins.

skar mda' ltung ba.gloss: falling of a meteor; shower of meteors

senses.gloss: falling of a meteor; shower of meteors
senses.context: Renders Sanskrit ulkāpāta (also bhraṣṭolkā), literally the falling or dropping of a shooting star. Used of meteors falling from the sky, and glossed by Conze as a 'shower of meteors', typically among portents or omens.
Renders Sanskrit tārakopama-kalpa, an aeon named for its resemblance to the stars. Conze identifies it as the period (kalpa) associated with the Tathāgata Suvarṇapuṣpa.

skar ma'i tshogs.gloss: host of stars; collection of stars

senses.gloss: host of stars; collection of stars
senses.context: Renders Sanskrit tāraka-gaṇa, tāragaṇa, jyotirgaṇa, and tārānikara, i.e., a multitude or assemblage of stars or heavenly luminaries. Rendered variously as 'collection of stars', 'group of stars', or 'host of stars'.

see_also: skar ma lta bu'i bskal pa

skal mnyam gyi rgyu.gloss: cause of equal lot; cause of similar lot

senses.gloss: cause of equal lot; cause of similar lot
senses.context: Renders Sanskrit sabhāga-hetu, a type of cause classified in Abhidharma-style enumerations of causes. Named from the fact that cause and effect share the same 'lot' or class (skal mnyam pa, sabhāga).

skal mnyam pa.gloss: of equal lot; of similar share

senses.gloss: of equal lot; of similar share
senses.context: Renders Sanskrit sabhāga (abstract sabhāgatā), said of those sharing the same lot, share, or fortune, i.e., belonging to a common class. This term underlies the designation of the sabhāga-hetu, the cause of equal lot.

skal don.gloss: supersensory object; object hidden (from ordinary perception)

senses.gloss: supersensory object; object hidden (from ordinary perception)
senses.context: Glossed by Hopkins as a "supersensory object," i.e. an object not accessible to ordinary sense perception. Lokesh Chandra records the equivalent under the alternate spelling bskal don, suggesting the two orthographies are treated as variants of a single term.
The allotted portion or share that falls to someone; Hopkins gives "lot, share." Related forms such as skal pa can ("having the share") build on this sense.
Rendered by Hopkins as "fortune," and equated by Lokesh Chandra with Sanskrit adṛṣṭa (the "unseen" allotment or destiny) — one's fortune as what has been apportioned to one.
Lokesh Chandra also records the Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra equivalent bhavya, in the sense of one who is fit or suitable, i.e. possessed of the requisite endowment.

see_also: skal pa rab tu gyur pa

skal pa can.gloss: having the lot; having the share; fortunate

senses.gloss: having the lot; having the share; fortunate
senses.context: Possessive form of skal pa, glossed by Hopkins as "having the lot, having the share, having the fortune." Lokesh Chandra cites bhāgīya and bhāgin, both formed from bhāga ("share, portion"), i.e. one who possesses a share or portion.
Lokesh Chandra also gives bhavya, indicating one who is fit or suitably endowed — possessed of the requisite qualification.

see_also: skal pa rab tu gyur pa

senses.context: Compound of skal pa (lot, share, fortune) with bzang po (good); Lokesh Chandra gives Sanskrit subhaga, "of good fortune, blessed."
Hopkins renders the term as "auspicious age," i.e. a fortunate period or era, the good lot of a particular time.

see_also: skal pa rab tu gyur pa

senses.context: Formed from skal pa (lot, share, fortune) intensified by rab tu gyur pa (become supremely so); Hopkins renders it "most fortunate." It designates one whose allotted fortune is of the highest degree.

Renders Sanskrit yathā-bhavyam, expressing that something is allotted or distributed as befits the recipient's share. Hopkins glosses it in Perfection of Wisdom contexts as 'which corresponds to the merit', i.e. proportionate to what one is due or fit for.

skal ba mnyam pa.gloss: having an equal lot; equal share

senses.gloss: having an equal lot; equal share
senses.context: Corresponds to Sanskrit sabhāgatā / sahabhavyatā, the state of sharing the same portion or fortune as another. Hopkins gives 'having equal lot'.
In Perfection of Wisdom materials the term is rendered 'companionship', i.e. the condition of those who share a common lot or class.
Negative of skal ba, corresponding to Sanskrit abhavya / abhāgya. Hopkins gives 'without the lot; without the fortune', i.e. not endowed with the requisite share or good fortune.
In Perfection of Wisdom contexts the same term is rendered 'impossible; unable; unfit; uncapable', reflecting abhavya as lacking the capacity or eligibility for something.
Attested only through Hopkins' provisional English gloss 'backbone'; here skal is not the usual 'lot, share' but part of an anatomical term.
Hopkins gives the provisional gloss 'dowry', i.e. the portion or share sent along with a bride. The element skal reflects the sense of an allotted share.

sku dang gsung dang thugs sprul pa.gloss: emanations of exalted body, speech, and mind

senses.gloss: emanations of exalted body, speech, and mind
senses.context: A compound naming the emanations (sprul pa, nirmāṇa) manifested by way of the exalted body, speech, and mind (kāya-vāk-citta) of a buddha. Attested in Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra literature as kāya-vāk-citta-nirmāṇa.

Renders Sanskrit sat-kāya, the 'real' or 'existing' body, i.e. the individual body or individuality taken as genuine. Here sku (honorific 'body') is qualified by dam pa in the sense of true or genuine, matching the sat- element.
A set of seven regions or points of the body, glossed simply as 'seven body areas'; the comparanda give no further specification of the members of the set.

A representation of a holy body (sku) — literally 'body-likeness' — corresponding to Sanskrit pratimā, mūrti, and pratibimba, i.e. an image, statue, or reflected likeness serving as a religious object.
In the sense of Sanskrit pratinidhi, something standing in place of the original; the image functions as a surrogate for the person or body it depicts.
Honorific term for the shoulder, formed from sku ('body', hon.) plus dpung ('shoulder'), hence the literal analysis 'body-shoulder'.

sku blugs.gloss: cast image, metal statue (of a holy being)

senses.gloss: cast image, metal statue (of a holy being)
senses.context: Honorific term for a representation of the body (sku) of a buddha or other venerated figure, made by pouring (blugs) molten metal into a mould. Rendered by Hopkins as 'metal image'.

sku blugs ma.gloss: cast image, metal statue (of a holy being)

senses.gloss: cast image, metal statue (of a holy being)
senses.context: Feminine/nominalized form equivalent to sku blugs, glossed by Hopkins as 'metal image', i.e. an honorific body-image produced by casting molten metal.
Negation of sku (honorific 'body'), corresponding to Sanskrit akāya. Used of that which lacks or is devoid of a body.
Literally 'body-life being long'; the honorific expression for longevity, corresponding to Sanskrit dīrgha-āyuṣkatā, 'long life'.
Literally 'body-equal', i.e. one who is a match or equal to the honored person; the honorific term for a wife or husband.
Rendered by Sanskrit maṇḍalagātratā, i.e. the quality of the body being well-rounded or circular in outline; kho lag indicates the encircling contour or girth of the sku.

senses.gloss: outer limit, boundary (of a maṇḍala/round form)
senses.context: Corresponding to maṇḍala-paryanta, the outermost edge or limit of a round form or maṇḍala; Hopkins glosses simply 'boundary' (C).

sku la dbang 'byor ba nyid.gloss: attainment of mastery over the body

senses.gloss: attainment of mastery over the body
senses.context: For Sanskrit kāya-vibhutva (MSA): the state of having sovereignty or command with respect to the [exalted] body. The final nyid marks it as the abstract state or quality of such mastery.
Title of a work of praise directed to the three exalted bodies (sku gsum), Sanskrit Kāyatrayastotra; attributed to Nāgārjuna (P2015, vol. 46).
For Sanskrit kāyācintya (MSA): the [buddha's] body as beyond the reach of thought, i.e. not encompassable by conceptual mind (bsam gyis mi khyab = acintya).

sku'i khyad par.gloss: distinguishing feature of the exalted body

senses.gloss: distinguishing feature of the exalted body
senses.context: For Sanskrit kāya-viśeṣa (MSA): a special attribute or distinctive quality pertaining to the sku, rendered by Hopkins as 'attribute/feature of exalted body'.
In less honorific application, the particular bodily or physical characteristic that distinguishes one thing from another.

see_also: sku dang gsung dang thugs sprul pa

senses.context: Rendered by Sanskrit kāya-karman (MSA), the deeds or actions performed through the body. Used honorifically (sku, phrin las) of the enlightened body's activities, hence 'exalted physical activity'.

see_also: sku dang gsung dang thugs sprul pa

senses.context: Past form of skur ('debs), glossed as to deprecate, depreciate, or deny. Used of denying or disparaging what exists or is the case.
Corresponds to Sanskrit apodya (C), glossed as going away from or withdrawing from, and hence negating. As a Tibetan phrase it is a past/completed form of skur pa 'debs, to deprecate or deny.

Appearing also as bskul and related spellings, this corresponds to Sanskrit codana (urging, prompting) and preraka (one who impels), with the sense of rousing, entreating, or urging someone on. Also attested for parikṣeptṛ and helā.
Continuative form (cing) of skul, corresponding to Sanskrit codayati (C), to urge, exhort, or prompt. In some contexts it carries the sense of warning against something or making a charge.
Name of a bird, the magpie. Attested only as an animal name in the comparanda.
Tibetan rendering of the Indian city name Pāṭaliputra, given as such by Das, Lokesh Chandra, and Hopkins. Used as a proper name, not as an analyzable compound.

Descriptive phrase indicating that something has been thoroughly churned or stirred with a paddle or churning stick (skya ba). Occurs as a simile-like expression rather than a technical term in the comparanda.

skya ser gnyis.gloss: ordained and lay people; the two, lay and ordained

senses.gloss: ordained and lay people; the two, lay and ordained
senses.context: An enumerative compound ('the two, white and yellow') designating the laity together with the ordained, i.e. the whole community of practitioners. Hopkins glosses it simply as 'ordained and lay people'.
The vows or restraints (sdom pa) undertaken in connection with going for refuge (skyabs 'gro). Glossed by Hopkins as 'refuge vows'.

Predicative expression corresponding to Sanskrit śaraṇatvānuttarya, the quality of being an unsurpassed refuge. In the Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra context it characterizes an object of refuge beyond which there is none higher.
Renders śaraṇa-gamanādhikāra, the section, topic, or occasion concerned with going for refuge. Used to mark the point in a text or practice at which refuge is taken.

skyabs su 'gro ba'i khyad par.gloss: features/distinctive qualities of going for refuge

senses.gloss: features/distinctive qualities of going for refuge
senses.context: Renders śaraṇa-pratipatti-viśeṣaṇa, the qualifying characteristics that distinguish the practice of going for refuge. Refers to what specifies or sets apart one mode of taking refuge from another.
The formal rite or liturgical procedure (cho ga) by which one goes for refuge. Hopkins gives it as a phrase-level rendering, 'ritual for taking refuge.'
Renders śaraṇa-gamana-vyavasāya, the firm determination or certainty regarding going for refuge. Hopkins glosses it as being definite or certain to go for refuge.

Rendering Sanskrit śaraṇa-vipravādana, this term names the condition of being thoroughly misled or deluded about what constitutes a refuge. It concerns error regarding the object of going for refuge rather than refuge itself.
A proper name corresponding to Sanskrit pāṇḍu, identified in the comparanda as Pāṇḍu, the father of the five Pāṇḍavas. Here the Tibetan functions as a name, not as a term of the refuge vocabulary.
A water bird, glossed in English as 'heron'; the Sanskrit comparandum given is amlikā. The form belongs with the related entries built on skyar.
Corresponds to Sanskrit paryaṅka, the cross-legged sitting posture. It appears as the shortened form of skyil mo krung and occurs in expressions for assuming or sitting in that posture.

Corresponds to Sanskrit paryaṅka (also cited as udrā), the cross-legged manner of sitting. The full form of skyil krung, it occurs in phrases describing assuming the posture and remaining seated in it.

see_also: skyil mo krung bcas te bzhugs so

senses.context: Instrumental/adverbial phrase built on skyil mo krung (cross-legged posture, paryaṅka), rendering eka-paryaṅkena: by means of one cross-legged session. Used of an act completed during a single uninterrupted sitting of cross-legged meditation.

skyu na gsal.gloss: it is clear in the run of the text

senses.gloss: it is clear in the run of the text
senses.context: A remark that the point at issue is evident from the flow or continuity of the passage itself, requiring no further comment. Only an English gloss is attested for this phrase; no Sanskrit equivalent is given.

Renders Sanskrit āmalakī / āmalaka (also ambla, amlaka, tiṣyaphalā, rucaka, dhātrī), glossed in English as 'olive' or 'sour medicinal fruit'. A sour fruit used in medicine, frequently named in materia medica lists.
Present/continuative form of skyug pa, corresponding to Sanskrit vamat, 'vomiting'; used also of something spurting or gushing out.
In some Prajñāpāramitā contexts the form is matched with āgacchati, 'comes (along), approaches, comes to'. This correspondence is attested only in the Conze materials.
Literally 'vomit-turning-out' (skyug + log pa), i.e. the upset or turning of the stomach that precedes vomiting. Only an English gloss is attested; no Sanskrit equivalent is given.

skyung ka.gloss: a black bird with a red beak (myna, jackdaw)

senses.gloss: a black bird with a red beak (myna, jackdaw)
senses.context: Name of a black bird distinguished by its red beak. Hopkins gives only this descriptive gloss, without further zoological specification.
Lokesh Chandra records bhagavatī opposite this headword. Since bhagavatī elsewhere corresponds to bcom ldan 'das ma, this equivalence is anomalous and should be checked against the source before use.

Standard rendering of Sanskrit amla/āmla, cukra, śukta, one of the tastes; the abstract amlatā gives the sense 'sourness, acidity.' Used both adjectivally of foods and substances and substantivally of the quality itself.
The equivalent apanud points to a verbal use, 'to cast off, expel, get rid of.' This sense is homonymous with the taste-term and must be determined from context.
A set of three characteristics—arising, remaining, and ceasing—by reference to which phenomena are classified. Hopkins renders dgag here as 'cessation' within this triad.

see_also: skye dgag gnas gsum mi rung ba'i chos
skye dgag gnas gsum rung ba'i chos

skye dgag gnas gsum mi rung ba'i chos.gloss: phenomenon for which production, abiding, and cessation are not possible

senses.gloss: phenomenon for which production, abiding, and cessation are not possible
senses.context: A phenomenon of which the three—production, abiding, and cessation—cannot be predicated, i.e. one to which that triad is unsuitable. Contrasted with the phenomena for which the same three are suitable.

see_also: skye dgag gnas gsum rung ba'i chos

skye dgag gnas gsum rung ba'i chos.gloss: phenomenon for which production, abiding, and cessation are suitable

senses.gloss: phenomenon for which production, abiding, and cessation are suitable
senses.context: A phenomenon of which the three—production, abiding, and cessation—are possible or fitting. Contrasted with phenomena for which that triad is not possible.

see_also: skye dgag gnas gsum mi rung ba'i chos

senses.context: Compound of skye dgu ("beings, creatures") with don ("aim, benefit, welfare"), used for actions or aspirations undertaken for the sake of [all] living beings.

Hopkins also records for this entry the gloss Prajāpati, name of the fourth lunar mansion, a value otherwise attaching to skye dgu'i bdag po ("lord of beings"). The comparanda given do not explain how this sense arises here.

see_also: skye dgu'i bdag po dang bcas pa'i lha rnams

senses.context: Literally "master (bdag po) of beings (skye dgu)," rendering Sanskrit prajāpati, the divine lord of creatures.
By extension the same name designates an asterism, glossed by Lokesh Chandra as rohiṇīnakṣatra and by Hopkins as the fourth constellation.

see_also: skye dgu'i bdag po dang bcas pa'i lha rnams

senses.context: Renders Sanskrit saprajāpatikā devā, a phrase for the assembled deities accompanied by, or gathered around, Prajāpati, the lord of beings.
Renders Sanskrit ṣaḍāyatana, the set of six āyatanas or sense-bases; skye mched is the standard equivalent of āyatana, "source, sense-sphere."
Renders Sanskrit āyatana-kauśalya, expertise or proficiency (mkhas pa) with respect to the sense-spheres (skye mched, āyatana).

Renders Sanskrit puruṣottama, an epithet of praise designating the highest or best among persons. Hopkins also records the renderings "supreme creature" and "supreme man," reflecting that skye can denote a born being generally as well as a human person.

Attested only through Hopkins' provisional English rendering "section of generation," i.e., a division or portion (thebs) belonging to production or generation (skye). No Sanskrit comparandum is supplied, so the technical scope of the term cannot be specified further here.

The enumerated form of skye thebs, given by Hopkins provisionally as "two sections of generation." Without a Sanskrit equivalent or further comparanda, only the fact of a twofold division of generation (skye) is established; the identity of the two members is not supplied.

A paired expression corresponding to Sanskrit janana-maraṇa, joining being born (skye) with dying ('chi). It names the two termini of an individual existence and thus the basic frame of transmigratory life.

skye po bdag 'dzin can.gloss: one who holds a self of the person; Proponent of Permanent Existence

senses.gloss: one who holds a self of the person; Proponent of Permanent Existence
senses.context: Literally one possessed of (can) apprehension ('dzin pa) of a self (bdag) of the person (skye po). Hopkins gives the provisional rendering "Proponent of Permanent Existence," indicating a party characterized by asserting such a self; the comparanda do not identify the school more precisely.

skye 'phreng.gloss: garland of lives, series of rebirths

senses.gloss: garland of lives, series of rebirths
senses.context: A 'rosary' or garland (phreng) of births, i.e. the sequence of one life after another. Used of the string of successive incarnations of a single continuum of lives.
Renders Sanskrit śukla-janman, literally a 'white' (dkar po) birth, i.e. a birth that is good or wholesome. The colour term marks the virtuous, positive character of the rebirth.

Renders upapatti-viśeṣaṃ prāpya: a phrase indicating that one has attained (thob nas) a distinguished or special (khyad par can) birth/rebirth. The gerund form marks the attained birth as the basis for what follows.
The nine classes or realms into which beings are born, taken as a set.
By extension, all those born in the nine-fold birth realms, hence 'many' or 'all' living beings; comparable in usage to skye dgu.

Renders utpatti-niḥsvabhāvatā, the absence of any own-nature (ngo bo nyid ma mchis pa) with respect to production or arising (skye ba). It designates the naturelessness of [self-]production, i.e. that things do not arise by way of their own nature.

skye ba dang mthun pa.gloss: concordant with production; conducive to birth

senses.gloss: concordant with production; conducive to birth
senses.context: Renders Sanskrit utpatty-anukūla, 'in accord with (favorable to) arising.' Used of what is concordant with, or conducive to, birth or production.
Corresponds to Sanskrit cayāpārthya, indicating production or birth that serves no purpose. The term marks arising that is meaningless or without aim.
Renders catur-daśa-vidha utpādaḥ, a fourteenfold enumeration of modes of birth or production. Used as a set category in Mahāyāna scholastic listings.
Translates Sanskrit jantu, a born being or creature; in some contexts the Sanskrit is explained as referring to lower creatures such as scorpions and the like, hence the rendering 'vermin.'

Appears among the terms grouped with self (ātman), sentient being (sattva), life-principle (jīva), and person (pudgala) in the list of views of a self. In this use it names one of the conventional designations mistakenly taken as a real self.
An emanation body (sprul sku) manifested as a birth or incarnation. Glossed simply as 'incarnation emanation body'; no Sanskrit equivalent is supplied in the comparanda.

skye ba 'phongs shing.gloss: having passed through this present birth; after death

senses.gloss: having passed through this present birth; after death
senses.context: Rendered by Sanskrit jāti-vyativṛtta (glossed as janma-antara-gata, 'gone to another birth,' and sva-prakṛti-parityāga, 'abandoning one's own nature'), the phrase marks the point at which the present life has been left behind. Hopkins gives '(after they have) passed through this present birth (life); after one has died.'
For Sanskrit anutpāda-vijñāpanatā, the term denotes the making known or communicating of non-production (skye ba med pa). Hopkins: 'it is informed about non-production.'
The comparandum anupapadyamāna supports the reading 'without ever being reborn,' i.e. no (further) birth taking place.
Sanskrit anupapatti, glossed by Hopkins as 'no rebirth.' The phrase negates skye ba in the sense of birth into existence.
A paired expression corresponding to Sanskrit anupāda-upāda (as cited), i.e. the absence of arising together with arising. Hopkins: 'non-production and production.'

Corresponds to Sanskrit anutpādādi, introducing non-production as the first member of a series. Hopkins also allows 'no production and so forth' and 'birthless and so forth,' reflecting the two senses of skye ba as production and as birth.

Rendered in Sanskrit as jñānājāti (Mahāvyutpatti), i.e. knowledge concerned with the absence of (further) production or birth. Hopkins glosses it as 'knowledge of no more birth', suggesting the realization that no further rebirth will take place.

skye ba med pa'i chos la bzod pa.gloss: forbearance with respect to the doctrine of non-production

senses.gloss: forbearance with respect to the doctrine of non-production
senses.context: A term for the capacity to bear or accept the teaching that phenomena are not (truly) produced. Hopkins offers the alternatives forbearance / patience / tolerance / endurance with regard to the doctrine of non-production (skye ba med pa'i chos).

Corresponds to Sanskrit hīnopapattiḥ śritā (Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra), 'relying on an inferior rebirth.' The phrase describes something that rests upon or is bound up with a lowly, inferior mode of birth.
Corresponds to Sanskrit janma-kṣaya (Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra), the exhaustion or wearing away of (re)birth. Hopkins gives 'extinction of birth.'
Corresponds to Sanskrit śubha-janman and śobhana ... janman (Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra). Used of a birth that is fine, fortunate, or auspicious, in contrast to an inferior one.

A paired negation (Skt. notpādo na nirodhaḥ) denying both arising and ceasing of a phenomenon. Used to characterize what is free of the extremes of coming into being and passing away; renderable as 'no production and also no cessation' or 'both no production and no cessation'.
Said of one whose taking of birth or rebirth is fixed or certain (Skt. upapatti-niyatipāta), i.e., destined to fall into a particular birth.
Production or accumulation that serves no aim (Skt. cayāpārthya). The phrase marks an arising as lacking purpose or meaning.

The class of afflictive defilement associated with birth or coming into existence (Skt. janma-saṃkleśa, utpatti-saṃkleśa, utpāda-saṃkleśa). Occurs as one member of enumerations of types of thorough affliction.

skye ba'i skad cig ma dang po phyin chad.gloss: from the first moment of birth onward

senses.gloss: from the first moment of birth onward
senses.context: A temporal expression (Skt. prathama-janma-kṣaṇād ūrdhvam) marking the span beginning with the initial instant of birth and continuing thereafter.

skye ba'i sgo.gloss: door of production; door of birth

senses.gloss: door of production; door of birth
senses.context: Renders Sanskrit āya-dvāra, the 'door' or gateway through which arising/birth takes place. Used for that which serves as the opening or avenue for something being produced or born.

skye ba'i sgo bcom pa.gloss: destroying the door of production; destroying the possibility (of arising)

senses.gloss: destroying the door of production; destroying the possibility (of arising)
senses.context: Literally 'demolishing the door of birth/production'; glossed by Hopkins as 'destroying the possibility'. The image is of blocking or wrecking the gateway through which arising or rebirth could occur.

skye ba'i chos can.gloss: subject to production; having the nature of arising

senses.gloss: subject to production; having the nature of arising
senses.context: Renders utpāda-dharmin, said of what possesses the quality (chos can) of being produced, i.e. what is liable to arise. Used to characterize phenomena that are produced rather than unproduced.

Renders janma-nirmāṇakāya, an emanation body (sprul sku) associated with taking birth; Hopkins renders it 'construction emanation body'. The comparanda identify it only as a type of nirmāṇakāya specified by skye ba (birth/production).

skye ba'i phreng ba.gloss: garland of lives; sequence of rebirths

senses.gloss: garland of lives; sequence of rebirths
senses.context: A 'rosary' or string (phreng ba) of births, i.e. successive lives or incarnations taken in sequence. Used for an unbroken series of embodiments.

skye ba'i lus bor te sprul pa'i lus 'dzi.gloss: having abandoned the body of birth, to assume an emanation body

senses.gloss: having abandoned the body of birth, to assume an emanation body
senses.context: A descriptive phrase (Skt. janma-kāyaṃ tyaktvā nirmāṇa-kāyaṃ gṛhṇāti) for setting aside the body produced by ordinary birth (skye ba'i lus) and taking on instead an emanated or manifested body (sprul pa'i lus). Attested in Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra materials.
A person of bad character; Skt. durjana, duṣṭajana, khala, asatyajana. Used of persons who are wicked, dishonest, or malicious, in contrast to the good.
Keeping company or dwelling with evil people (Skt. kujana-vāsa). Typically cited among conditions to be avoided, since consorting with bad beings is harmful.
Sympathy or mercy (rjes su brtse ba) directed toward persons who are beset by the afflictions (nyon mongs pa); Skt. kliṣṭajanānukampā. Attested in Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra materials.
Dwelling or keeping company with beings who are hostile and ill-natured (Skt. duṣṭa-jana-vāsa). Parallel in form and use to skye bo ngan pa dang 'grogs pa, association with bad persons.

skye bo phal cher.gloss: most beings; the majority of people

senses.gloss: most beings; the majority of people
senses.context: Formed from skye bo (person, being; Skt. jana) with phal cher (most, the greater part), the term designates people in general — the majority or the common run of beings. Hopkins accordingly renders it 'most beings', and in contexts where jana is a collective it may be understood as 'people' or a crowd of people.
Skt. mūrkha-jana, from mūrkha (stupid, foolish) qualifying jana (person, being). Attested in the Madhyāntavibhāga material as a designation for beings characterized by stupidity.

skye bo mang po dga' ba.gloss: dear to many beings; liking many beings

senses.gloss: dear to many beings; liking many beings
senses.context: Corresponds to Skt. bahu-jana-supriya, literally 'very dear to many people'. Hopkins glosses the Tibetan as 'liking many beings', reflecting that the Tibetan construction (skye bo mang po dga' ba) can be read either as affection felt toward many beings or, following the Sanskrit, as being beloved of many; the comparanda do not settle the direction of the relation.
Skt. vimūḍha ... jana, i.e. a person (jana) who is bewildered or deluded (vimūḍha). Attested in Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra material and rendered by Hopkins as 'confused being'.

skye bo mdza' ba la byams pa.gloss: love for dear ones; loving friendly beings

senses.gloss: love for dear ones; loving friendly beings
senses.context: Corresponds to Skt. priya-jana-preman, 'affection (preman) for dear/beloved persons (priya-jana)'. The Tibetan renders priya-jana as skye bo mdza' ba, beings who are friends or dear ones, and preman as byams pa, love or affection directed toward them.

skyed mos tshal gyi sa.gloss: grounds of a pleasure-grove; site of a park

senses.gloss: grounds of a pleasure-grove; site of a park
senses.context: Compound of skyed mos tshal (pleasure grove, park) with sa (ground, place), corresponding to Sanskrit udyāna-bhūmi. Used for the location or plot of ground on which a garden or park stands.
Rendering Sanskrit udyāna (pleasure garden, park) and upavana (grove near a settlement), i.e. a cultivated or planted pleasure ground.
Also given for Sanskrit nikuñja, a shady thicket or arbour of trees and creepers.
Adjectival sense corresponding to Sanskrit āśu, java (speed, swiftness) and vikramin (striding, vigorous). Synonymous with myur ba and mgyogs pa.
Adverbial use corresponding to Sanskrit śīghram, kṣipram; glossed 'soon, quickly, speedily', and in imperative contexts 'hurry up with'.

The illustrative Tibetan citation itself writes rkyen bu (rnga mo des 'di ni rkyen bu zhig go snyam du shes te, 'the camel understood, thinking, "this is just a [mere] circumstance/reason"'), so skyen bu appears as an orthographic variant of rkyen bu. Glossed 'reason'.

skyen bu.sanskrit: rnga mo des 'di ni rkyen bu zhig go snyam du shes te

skyem tsam re.gloss: just briefly, for just a moment

senses.gloss: just briefly, for just a moment
senses.context: Adverbial phrase glossed 'just briefly'; the delimiting tsam re ('merely, just a little') marks a very short span. The comparanda give no Sanskrit equivalent.

skyes 'phreng.gloss: garland of lives, sequence of rebirths

senses.gloss: garland of lives, sequence of rebirths
senses.context: A 'string' or 'garland' (phreng) of births (skyes), i.e. a series of successive lives or incarnations. Used of the linked sequence of a being's rebirths, and hence of accounts arranged as such a series.
Rendering Sanskrit puruṣapudgala, a compound pairing two terms for 'person' (skyes bu = puruṣa; gang zag = pudgala). It denotes simply a person or individual being.
A person of the lesser (chung ngu) level of capacity or scope, but qualified as 'special' (khyad par can) within that level. The term presupposes a graded ranking of practitioners by capacity.

skyes bu chung ngu khyad par can gyi lam.gloss: path of a special being of small capacity

senses.gloss: path of a special being of small capacity
senses.context: The path (lam) belonging to, or traversed by, a special being of small capacity (skyes bu chung ngu khyad par can). It designates the stage of practice appropriate to that graded level of capacity.

skyes bu chung ngu dang thun mong pa'i l.gloss: path shared with beings of lesser capacity

senses.gloss: path shared with beings of lesser capacity
senses.context: A path (lam) held in common (thun mong) with those of small or lesser capacity (skyes bu chung ngu), i.e. practices not exclusive to higher-capacity persons but shared with them.

A designation within the graded classification of practitioners (beings of small, middling, and great capacity) for a distinguished or particular subtype of the being of small capacity, marked by 'khyad par can' (special, distinguished). The comparanda give only the phrase itself, without further specification of what makes such a being 'special'.

skyes bu chung 'bring thun mong gi lam.gloss: path in common with beings of small and middling capacity

senses.gloss: path in common with beings of small and middling capacity
senses.context: Refers to a portion of the path that is shared with, or held in common by, practitioners classed as beings of small capacity and beings of middling capacity. The term presupposes the threefold division of beings into small, middling, and great capacity.

skyes bu che 'bring thun mong gi lam.gloss: path in common with beings of great and middling capacity

senses.gloss: path in common with beings of great and middling capacity
senses.context: Refers to a portion of the path that is shared with, or held in common by, practitioners classed as beings of middling capacity and beings of great capacity. As with the parallel term for small and middling beings, it presupposes the threefold classification of practitioners by capacity.
Translates Sanskrit mohapuruṣa: a person characterized by delusion or bewilderment (gti mug). Glossed also as beclouded, ignorant, confused, or befuddled.

Corresponds to Sanskrit satpuruṣa-saṃsevā, satpuruṣāśraya/satpuruṣāpāśraya: attending upon, associating with, or taking as one's support a true, holy, or excellent person (skyes bu dam pa). Rendered variously as relying on or acquainting oneself with a holy, excellent, or true being.

see_also: skyes mchog ka lo sgyur ba

skyes bu dam pa'i las byed pa.gloss: performing the actions of a holy being

senses.gloss: performing the actions of a holy being
senses.context: Renders Sanskrit satpuruṣa-karma-karaṇatā (MSA): the state of carrying out the deeds proper to a holy, excellent, or true being (satpuruṣa, skyes bu dam pa). Used of conduct that matches the standard of such an exemplary person.

see_also: skyes mchog ka lo sgyur ba

senses.context: Renders Sanskrit puruṣa-kāra-phala (MSA, MV): a fruit or effect produced through a person's own agency or effort (puruṣakāra), as distinguished from results not brought about by personal action.
Corresponds to Sanskrit avidagdha, a person lacking discernment or maturity of mind.
In Conze's usage (C) it renders mohapuruṣa, a person under the sway of delusion (moha).

skyes bu 'bring gi lam.gloss: path of a being of middling capacity

senses.gloss: path of a being of middling capacity
senses.context: Renders Sanskrit madhyapuruṣamārga: the path suited to a practitioner of intermediate ('bring) capacity, implicitly contrasted with paths for lesser and greater types of persons.

see_also: skyes mchog ka lo sgyur ba

senses.context: A person who is bewildered or deluded (rmongs pa). Attested in Hopkins only as a proposed rendering, without a Sanskrit equivalent.

skyes bu tshad ma.gloss: valid person, one who has become an authority

senses.gloss: valid person, one who has become an authority
senses.context: Renders Sanskrit pramāṇabhūta, literally 'one who has become a valid means of knowledge' (pramāṇa), i.e. a being whose word or attainment is authoritative. Hopkins glosses it as 'valid person/being'.

skyes bu gsum ka.gloss: beings of the three capacities, all three types of persons

senses.gloss: beings of the three capacities, all three types of persons
senses.context: A collective term (gsum ka, 'all three') for the threefold classification of practitioners according to capacity or scope. Hopkins gives the tentative rendering 'beings of the three capacities'; no Sanskrit comparandum is supplied.

skyes bu'i rgyud kyis bsdus pa'i rdul du.gloss: atomically established phenomenon included within a being's continuum

senses.gloss: atomically established phenomenon included within a being's continuum
senses.context: A technical division of that which is established as (composed of) particles, distinguishing what belongs to the mental-physical continuum (rgyud) of a person from what does not. Hopkins: 'that which is atomically established and is included within the continuum of a being.'

skyes bu'i rgyud kyis ma bsdus pa'i rdul.gloss: atomically established phenomenon not included within a being's continuum

senses.gloss: atomically established phenomenon not included within a being's continuum
senses.context: The complementary member of the twofold division of that which is established as (composed of) particles: matter not belonging to the continuum of any person. Hopkins: 'that which is atomically established and is not included within the continuum of a being.'

skyes bu'i mthu.gloss: human effort, personal power, manly action

senses.gloss: human effort, personal power, manly action
senses.context: Rendering Sanskrit puruṣakāra, the strength or exertion proper to a person. Hopkins, following Conze's usages, glosses it as '(manly) doing' or 'work'.

skyes bu'i 'dod pa tsam gyis bzhag pa'i.gloss: relation established merely by a person's wish

senses.gloss: relation established merely by a person's wish
senses.context: A connection between things that holds not by nature but only because a speaker or agent posits it intentionally. Glossed as a relation established by the mere intention of the speaker.
The stream of consciousness belonging to a person (skyes bu); used as the frame of reference for what does or does not belong to an individual's mind-stream.

skyes bu'i shes rgyud kyis bsdus pa'i gz.gloss: form included within a being's mental continuum

senses.gloss: form included within a being's mental continuum
senses.context: Form (gzugs) that is subsumed within the mind-stream of a person, i.e. counted as belonging to that individual's continuum. Contrasts with form not so included.

skyes bu'i shes rgyud kyis ma bsdus pa'i.gloss: form not included within a being's mental continuum

senses.gloss: form not included within a being's mental continuum
senses.context: Form (gzugs) that is not subsumed within the mind-stream of a person, i.e. not counted as part of that individual's continuum. The complement of form included within a being's mental continuum.

skyes bu'i shes rgyud bsdus pa.gloss: included within a being's mental continuum

senses.gloss: included within a being's mental continuum
senses.context: Said of what is contained or subsumed within the mind-stream of a person. Used as a classificatory qualification, notably of forms.

skyes bu'i shes rgyud ma bsdus pa.gloss: not included within the mental continuum of a person

senses.gloss: not included within the mental continuum of a person
senses.context: A qualifying phrase used of something that is not contained in (not subsumed under) the mind-stream (shes rgyud) of a being or person (skyes bu). Hopkins renders it 'not contained within the mental continuum of a being'.

skyes bus byed pa'i 'bras bu.gloss: effect made by a person; personally made effect

senses.gloss: effect made by a person; personally made effect
senses.context: An effect ('bras bu) characterized as being produced by a person or agent (skyes bu). Hopkins glosses the phrase as 'personally made effect'.

skyes zin pa yang skye ba ni ma yin.gloss: what has already been produced is not produced again

senses.gloss: what has already been produced is not produced again
senses.context: A stock formula denying re-production of what is already produced, corresponding to Sanskrit (MSA) utpannaṃ punar utpadyate (na-). The Tibetan uses skyes zin pa ('what has already arisen') as subject of the negated verb skye ba.

skyes zin pa yang skye ba ni ma yin.sanskrit: skye/ skye/ skyes/ skyes/; {MSA}utpannaṃ punar utpadyate (na-)

senses.context: Hopkins supplies only a tentative gloss ({PH}) 'quarrel'; no Sanskrit equivalent is attested in the comparanda, so the rendering should be treated as provisional.

skyo bcas sems can smin par byed.gloss: ripening sentient beings who are dispirited (or in distress)

senses.gloss: ripening sentient beings who are dispirited (or in distress)
senses.context: Corresponds to Sanskrit (MSA) sodvegā sattva-pācanā, 'the ripening of sentient beings accompanied by udvega (weariness, agitation, disquiet)'. Hopkins renders it 'ripening poor sentient beings', taking skyo bcas as the qualification of the beings being matured.
